site.headline: Researcher in computer networks and distributed systems, with experience building and shipping software.

featured.title: AgenTraffic: how teams of AI agents load the network
featured.problem: When several AI agents work together, does the way they are organised change the load they put on servers and networks?
featured.did: Built a test setup that runs the same team of agents in three arrangements (one after another, through a coordinator, and everyone talking to everyone) and measures the traffic at every level, from the application down to the network.
featured.outcome: It does: when one agent hands work to several others, requests arrive in bursts that the standard traffic model cannot describe. Published as lead author at NAIC 2026 @ ACM SIGCOMM.

featured.title: Building and running an analytics product
featured.problem: A new analytics product for banks and investment firms had to win its first clients and pass a security audit while it was still being built.
featured.did: I now work on it as both software engineer and technical product manager. Before that, I got its first clients set up and running.
items: Run the product side of the team's internal tools and AI work: priorities, scope agreed with the firm's AI teams, and planning
Built automated tests that every release must pass, which greatly reduced manual checking
Automated how the product is built, tested and released
Helped move the product's data to a new database setup (PostgreSQL and Amazon Athena) for more reliable, faster queries
Built real-time monitoring and dashboards on AWS
Built Excel add-ins and early interface prototypes for the product

featured.title: Edge-Healer: servers that repair themselves offline
featured.problem: Servers at remote sites rely on a central controller to restart apps that crash. If the connection to it drops, a crashed app stays down until the link comes back.
featured.did: Built a small agent that runs on every server. The servers keep each other updated on their health and spare capacity, and when an app crashes they agree among themselves which one restarts it.
featured.outcome: Designed to recover in under a second, and to tidy up any duplicates once the connection returns. The paper, poster and an interactive demo are on the project site.

featured.title: Context-Aware HPA: scaling services on the load coming at them
featured.problem: Kubernetes scales each service on its own load, so in a chain of services the ones further down only react after the traffic has already reached them.
featured.did: Second author on the research. I built the test setup: a standard social-network benchmark on a Kubernetes cluster, with monitoring and load tests, and a scaler where each service reacts to the load arriving at the service before it.
featured.outcome: Cut the slowest 1% of response times by 9.88% on the benchmark. A paper is in preparation, with Berta Serracanta as first author.

featured.title: Agentic DevOps: managing a team of AI coding agents
featured.problem: One person directing many AI coding agents on the same codebase needs their work to stay easy to review and combine, and to carry on when usage limits interrupt it.
featured.did: Built a Claude Code plugin that gives a lead agent the tools to start helper agents, check and merge their work, and hand over to a fresh session. Its safety rules cannot be skipped, and overnight runs restart on their own.
featured.outcome: Used to build Margin. Reviewing each piece of work before merging it caught serious bugs in about half of them.

featured.title: A training app with a built-in AI coach
featured.problem: Logging training has to take seconds on a phone, and an AI coach is only useful if it can see that data.
featured.did: Designed and built the whole app: a fast phone interface that also works offline, a backend on Cloudflare, and a direct connection that lets Claude read and update the training data. Automated agents review each day and fix the most important reported bugs.
featured.outcome: Runs at no cost on free plans. Every change is tested and released automatically, and anyone can try the full app in the browser with sample data.
